statement: The function returns a result r (so it does not fail), and the following holds. Call a target-subsequence any choice of indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j and nums[i_0] + ... + nums[i_{k-1}] = target; its length is k (the empty choice, k = 0, is allowed). Then either r = -1 and no target-subsequence exists, or 1 <= r <= len(nums), some target-subsequence has length r, and every target-subsequence has length at most r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: The function returns a result r on every input satisfying the preconditions; in particular it does not panic, overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, r <= target.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, there exist indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{r-1} such that 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j and nums[i_0] + ... + nums[i_{r-1}] = target.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, for every choice of indices i_0 < i_1 < ... < i_{k-1} with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j and nums[i_0] + ... + nums[i_{k-1}] = target, we have k <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = -1 if and only if there is no choice of indices i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} (possibly k = 0) with 0 <= i_j < len(nums) for all j and nums[i_0] + ... + nums[i_{k-1}] = target.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: If the sum of all entries of nums is strictly less than target, then the function returns -1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: If the sum of all entries of nums is exactly target, then the function returns len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: If len(nums) = 1, then the function returns 1 when nums[0] = target and returns -1 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: If target = 1, then the function returns 1 if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 1, and returns -1 otherwise.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: If nums[i] = 1 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), then the function returns target when target <= len(nums), and returns -1 when target > len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: For every slice ys with len(ys) = len(nums) and 1 <= ys[i] <= 1000 for all i, if ys is a permutation of nums (meaning there is a bijection pi on {0,...,len(nums)-1} such that ys[pi(i)] = nums[i] for all i), then whenever the function returns r on nums and r' on ys with the same target, r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.

statement: Let ys be any slice with len(ys) <= 1000 and 1 <= ys[j] <= 1000 for every j, such that nums occurs as a subsequence of ys (equivalently, ys can be obtained from nums by inserting zero or more elements). If the function returns r on nums and r' on ys with the same target, then r' >= r, where -1 is smaller than every nonnegative result.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 1000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] and nums[i] <= 1000; and 1 <= target and target <= 1000.
